newsitem.title: UK: Researchers home in on genes for asthma.
newsitem.headline: Researchers home in on genes for asthma.

text.p: British researchers said on Wednesday they were homing in on a genetic link to asthma.
William Cookson and colleagues at Oxford University said they had identified six potential places where genes for asthma might be.

Asthma, which affects one child in seven in Britain and is a growing problem in countries like the United States, Australia and New Zealand, is associated with allergic reactions in 95 percent of afflicted children.
Cookson's group looked at 80 Australian families with 200 children. Twelve percent were asthmatic and 52 percent showed allergic reactions of varying kinds.
The researchers then looked at the genetic make-up of their subjects and found six areas they seemed to have in common, although they stressed they had not identified any individual genes yet.
Genes sit on chromosomes, and there were chromosomal similarities in 75 percent of the children, the Oxford team reported in the science journal Nature.
One of the links, to chromosome 11q13, had been identified before but the rest were new, they said.
